title: Compose the approval policy contract into the daemon approval path
description:
CONSUMER EDGE for task-5d8f11c86a3a41b4a8a420ef0d52a444, which landed the contract as a PURE @moe/core module with NO consumer. Clause 1 requires this task to exist; it is the primary consumer.

WHAT LANDED AND IS READY TO COMPOSE (commit 18f0964, verify before planning — task rail 6 says a description's claims about disk are stale by default):
- packages/core/src/planning/approval-policy.ts — APPROVAL_POLICY_KINDS (frozen, ["PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN","REQUIRE_HUMAN"]), the ApprovalPolicy union with a REQUIRED delayMs on the auto arm, and decideApprovalAuthority(request) -> ApprovalAuthorityResult.
- packages/core/src/planning/approval-authority.ts — HumanAuthorityGate, HumanAuthorityGrant, grantHumanAuthority, APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_CODES (8), APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_LAYERS (2).
- All five values are published from the @moe/core ROOT (index-surface.test.ts pins 80).
- checkHumanAuthority and refuseApprovalAuthority are deliberately NOT published: decideApprovalAuthority is the only intended entry point, because it consults the gate FIRST by construction. Do not reach around it.

THE GAP THIS TASK CLOSES: nothing imports the contract. The daemon can still approve a plan with no policy consulted and no gate checked, which is the state the contract was written to end.

SCOPE: compose decideApprovalAuthority in front of the existing plan.approve path in apps/daemon, and persist the HumanAuthorityGate on the unit of work. approvePlan (packages/core/src/planning/planning-run-submission.ts:172) and its reducer arm (planning-run-reducer.ts:174) must keep their current behaviour for UNGATED work with their existing tests green and UNMODIFIED — the policy composes IN FRONT of them, it does not replace them.

CRITICAL, from the incident that motivated the contract: the gate must be persisted on the WORK'S OWN DURABLE IDENTITY, not as a lifecycle/status field. On 2026-08-15 a bulk promotion of every BLOCKED task cleared each task's recorded blockedReason; a gate stored like a status would have been cleared the same way. approval-authority.ts's module comment states this and is worth reading before designing the persistence.

FOR THE CONSUMER, a hazard the contract documents but cannot enforce: ApprovalAuthorityDecision.delayMs is a safe non-negative integer, which is WIDER than setTimeout accepts. A delay above 2**31-1 CLAMPS TO 1ms, so "effectively never" silently becomes "immediately". Bound it here, where the timer lives.

NOT IN SCOPE: the control-room surface (its own task), the orchestrator settings file (its own task), changing the contract itself.
definitionOfDone: The daemon's plan-approval path calls decideApprovalAuthority and honours its verdict; a gated unit of work cannot be approved through the daemon under any approval policy, proved by a test that drives the real daemon handler rather than the core function.
The HumanAuthorityGate is persisted on the unit of work's durable identity, and a test proves a bulk status transition does NOT clear it - the exact mechanism of the 2026-08-15 incident.
Every daemon-level refusal asserts the stable code AND the refusing layer from APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_CODES / APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_LAYERS, never merely that approval did not happen.
approvePlan and its plan.approve reducer arm keep their current behaviour for ungated work, with their existing tests green and unmodified.
delayMs is bounded before it reaches any timer, with a test pinning the behaviour above 2**31-1 rather than letting it clamp to 1ms.
A mutation drill removing the decideApprovalAuthority call turns a named daemon test red on its refusal assertion, restored byte-exact and verified by hash.
